title: What's In The Box
concept: Petersburg, Alaska has no data center, yet its Assembly is writing rules for one, and a private owner is still pursuing a small project at the old Ocean Beauty cannery. The draft pause tests grid capacity, generators and uncontained cooling, so it measures size, not what the machine runs. By the utility's own FAQ the full 2 MW build would use about sixteen cannery's worth a year, and its plan answered two of the three tests while grid capacity is not settled. A glass gauge named Grid stands in for the town's power system, a tarped crate for the unknown load, and a height chart for the question of how big.

fingerprint.palette: silver overcast fjord and spruce green with an ice-white glass gauge hero, golden fluid, a slate-violet tarp over the unknown load, a brown-rust cannery and one signal-crimson stamp
fingerprint.metaphor: a glass gauge measures a mystery crate against a growth chart on a rainy dock while a town council decides how tall is too tall

palette: silver overcast fjord and spruce green with an ice-white glass gauge hero, golden fluid, a slate-violet tarp over the unknown load, a brown-rust cannery and one signal-crimson stamp
divergence_note: The last films were tangerine walls over teal desks (11-06), a midnight indigo cab (11-02), an overcast moss slope (11-01), a sage chart desk (10-31) and an aubergine depot (10-29). This one is a rainy silver fjord dock in soft overcast light with an ice-white glass hero, a tarped crate and a wooden height chart. No office, cab, slope, depot or sea cutaway, and its signature object is a growth chart that changes state at every act boundary and lands with the pencil hovering and no line drawn.

treatment.title: What's In The Box
treatment.summary: Four pitches converged on the same hero (ReserveBar as Petersburg's grid) and the same honest spine, so the room judged on staging. The Comedian's tarped crate and height chart won scroll-stop and retention (a mystery object and a measurable question from frame one). Grafted: the Dramatist's three locks as the Gate rig and the 95s lock states, the Explainer's sixteen-cannery stack as the scale reveal, and the Enthusiast's honest narrowing (two locks answered by the utility's plan, grid capacity still open). Fairness: the utility's case gets a full named scene and the film never says the pause passed or that the facility is AI. Runner-ups folded in as the closing question.

angle.thesis: Petersburg isn't deciding whether it wants AI. It's deciding how big a single customer its 12.2 cent hydro grid should take on, and rules written for the load work whatever the racks run.
supporting_facts: Full 2 MW build would use 17,000,000 kWh a year, about 16x the cannery's 1,064,400 kWh in 2015 (c18-c20)
The pause's three triggers are physical: grid capacity, generators, uncontained cooling (c3); the record never says what the facility would compute (c28)
Assembly tied 3-3 on Sept 21, then unanimously approved a 9-month pause plus zoning rules Oct 5 (c7,c11,c13)
angle.counterpoint: The utility says the same load pays: over $2M a year and smaller rate increases at 12.2 cents (c21-c24), and the original plan already had no on-site diesel and closed loop cooling (c25,c26). A pause could cost that. Honest answer: rules set terms, grid capacity is the one trigger the record doesn't settle.
angle.falsifiable_by: A use-based trigger added to the rules, or a named workload that shifts the debate to what it computes.
runner_ups: Enthusiast: pause as spec sheet (folded in as counter-scene)
Skeptic: rules before knowing the workload (folded into the ending question)
guardrails: never say Petersburg's facility is AI; vendor marketing only
no causal link between deal falling through and votes

open_loop.what: What would the crate run? Planted when the tarp flinches, paid when the crowd turns from the crate to the chart and the film says the question is how big.

open_loop_2.what: Which of the three locks stays shut? Planted when the draft sheet pins up with three dotted lock outlines, paid when the grid capacity lock stays dark.
